switch_region_definitions.note: Regions are NOT taken from recall. Switch I is the UniProt annotation; Switch II is derived from the deposited secondary structure of the two files themselves.

switch_I.definition: UniProt P01116 feature type 'Motif', description 'Effector region'

switch_II.definition: operational: first residue after the end of strand beta-3 through the end of helix alpha-2, read from the deposited records of each file
switch_II.caveat: Literature ranges could not be verified verbatim (Europe PMC HTTP 503). The concept is attributable to Milburn et al., Science 1990, DOI 10.1126/science.2406906 (DOI verified via CrossRef); the switch-II pocket to Ostrem et al., Nature 2013, DOI 10.1038/nature12796 (DOI verified via CrossRef). sequence_alignment.method: Bio.Align.PairwiseAligner, global, BLOSUM62, open -11 / extend -1, on _entity_poly.pdbx_seq_one_letter_code_can
sequence_alignment.gap: 13-residue N-terminal His tag present only in 6OIM (unobserved in coordinates)

apo_holo_comparability.same_isoform_region: both cover UniProt residues 1-169, which are identical between KRAS4A and KRAS4B; the divergent hypervariable region (UniProt 166-185) is outside the modelled range for practical purposes
apo_holo_comparability.construct_difference: 4OBE = wild-type catalytic domain, native cysteines retained. 6OIM = G12C on a cysteine-light background (C51S/C80L/C118S) with a His tag.

the_difference.significance: the covalent anchor of the ligand does not exist in the apo input

superposition.method: Kabsch on CA atoms of the 166 common auth residues 1-169

blindness_assessment.question: Is the apo input 4OBE genuinely free of ligand in the Switch-II pocket region?
blindness_assessment.evidence: The only non-water heteroatoms in 4OBE are GDP (x2) and Mg2+ (x2). Their 4.5 A contact sets are the P-loop / nucleotide site (residues 11-18, 28-32, 116-120, 145-147) and the Mg site (17, 32, 33, 34, 36, 57). The intersection of the GDP+Mg contact sets with the 21-residue Switch-II pocket label set is {11, 12, 13, 16, 34} - all of which are P-loop residues shared between the nucleotide site and the S-IIP rim. Residues 58-63, 68, 69, 72 and 95-103 (the S-IIP proper) contact no ligand at all in 4OBE.

crypticity_test.method: superpose 4OBE chain onto 6OIM chain A on 166 common CA, apply the inverse transform to the 41 MOV heavy atoms, then measure closest approach to 4OBE protein heavy atoms
crypticity_test.interpretation: The pocket is fully closed in both apo copies. Met72, His95 and Arg68 occupy the volume the drug takes. This is the correct behaviour for a cryptic-site benchmark: no geometric cavity detector can find the site in the apo input, so the prediction is genuinely blind.

crystal_packing_at_pocket.method: REMARK 290 SMTRY operators from files.rcsb.org/download/4OBE.pdb, applied over unit-cell translations -1..+1

pipeline_breakers.finding: 4OBE is WILD-TYPE KRAS, not KRAS G12C. The challenge pairs it with a G12C holo structure.
pipeline_breakers.evidence: _struct_ref_seq_dif in data/raw/4OBE.cif has exactly 2 rows, both 'expression tag' GLY at auth 0; there is no mutation row. _atom_site.label_comp_id at auth_seq_id 12 is GLY in chains A and B. _struct.title is 'Crystal Structure of GDP-bound Human KRas'. RCSB reports mutation count 0 for the entity. UniProt P01116 residue 12 is G.
pipeline_breakers.mechanism: The ground-truth label set derived from 6OIM includes CYS12, the covalent anchor (S-gamma to MOV C25 at 1.805 A). That residue does not exist in the prediction input. Any per-residue scoring that treats residue 12 as a hit target is scoring a residue the model never saw in its oncogenic form. More seriously, the oncogenic mutation is the biological reason the pocket is druggable, so the apo input is not the apo form of the protein whose pocket we are predicting.
pipeline_breakers.affects: C1-adjacent: not a holo leak, but a target-identity mismatch that invalidates the biological framing of the benchmark.

pipeline_breakers.finding: The two entries are different constructs at four positions, three of them engineered cysteine removals absent from the apo.
pipeline_breakers.evidence: Pairwise global alignment of _entity_poly.pdbx_seq_one_letter_code_can: 166/170 identities (97.65%); mismatches at auth 12 (G/C), 51 (C/S), 80 (C/L), 118 (C/S). 6OIM _struct_ref_seq_dif labels 51, 80, 118 as 'engineered mutation'.
pipeline_breakers.mechanism: An elastic/contact network is built from side-chain and backbone contacts. C51S, C80L and C118S change side-chain volume and packing at three buried/semi-buried positions, so the apo network and the holo network are not networks of the same molecule. C80L in particular sits directly beneath the S-IIP floor region (alpha-3 face). Effect size is likely small but is not zero and is currently unquantified.
pipeline_breakers.affects: Comparability of predicted network to ground-truth pocket.

pipeline_breakers.finding: In 4OBE, 10 of the 21 Switch-II pocket residues make direct crystal contacts with a symmetry mate, and Switch II is anomalously rigid (B-factor 0.68-0.71x the chain mean).
pipeline_breakers.evidence: Symmetry expansion using REMARK 290 SMTRY operators: pocket residues 34, 59, 60, 61, 62, 63, 68, 69, 99, 103 lie within 4.5 A of symmetry-related protein atoms (closest TYR137 at 2.58 A, HIS94 at 2.59 A, ARG102 at 2.69 A). Mean B over auth 57-76 is 13.1 (chain A) against a chain mean of 18.5. In 6OIM the same 21 residues have zero crystal contacts and a B ratio of 1.18. Compare 4LDJ: only 2 of 21 in contact, B ratio 0.92.
pipeline_breakers.mechanism: The prediction path takes dynamics from topology. If the apo switch-II conformation is held by the lattice, the contact network encodes lattice-stabilised geometry rather than solution-state flexibility, and a method that ranks residues by predicted mobility or dynamic connectivity will systematically under-rank the very region it is meant to find. Residue 63, the largest apo/holo CA deviation (8.79 A), is itself in crystal contact.
pipeline_breakers.affects: R1 (first principles) and the physical validity of the elastic-network assumption C6 for this particular input.

pipeline_breakers.finding: 4OBE contains two protein copies in the asymmetric unit but the deposited biological assembly is a monomer, and the entry carries pseudo-translational symmetry.
pipeline_breakers.evidence: _entity.pdbx_number_of_molecules = 2 for entity 1; two _pdbx_struct_assembly rows, both oligomeric_details 'monomeric' (asym A,C,D,G and B,E,F,H). Chain A vs B CA RMSD 0.346 A, switch II mean deviation 0.10 A. Validation xtriage: off-origin Patterson peak 39.81% of origin, pseudo-translational symmetry.
pipeline_breakers.mechanism: Naive loading of the whole ASU builds a 338-node two-molecule network instead of a 169-node monomer, doubling the graph and creating spurious inter-copy edges. The copies are effectively identical (0.346 A), so nothing is gained. A chain must be chosen explicitly and recorded.
pipeline_breakers.affects: Determinism and the node set; trivially fixable but silently wrong if unhandled.

pipeline_breakers.finding: Neither structure is nucleotide-free. Both carry GDP + Mg2+.
pipeline_breakers.evidence: 4OBE entities 2 and 3: GDP x2, MG x2. 6OIM entities 2 and 3: MG x1, GDP x1. _struct_conn metalc rows show Mg coordinated by SER17.OG, the GDP beta-phosphate and four waters in both.
pipeline_breakers.mechanism: Not a defect - the nucleotide is the physiological ligand and the S-IIP is a separate site. But 'apo' here means drug-free, not ligand-free. Under C5 the nucleotide and Mg must be either dropped or modelled as simple nodes, and the choice recorded, because GDP contacts 19 residues including S-IIP rim residues 11, 12, 13, 16.

pipeline_breakers.finding: 6OIM has a 3-residue chain break at auth 105-107 that 4OBE does not have.
pipeline_breakers.mechanism: Only relevant if the ground-truth pipeline builds a network on the holo structure too. The break is outside both switch regions and outside the 21-residue pocket set, so the label set is unaffected.
pipeline_breakers.affects: Nothing in the current label-derivation procedure.

pipeline_breakers.finding: The apo Switch-II pocket is genuinely closed. This is a property to preserve, not a defect.
pipeline_breakers.evidence: MOV heavy atoms transplanted into the 4OBE frame clash at 0.74 A with MET72.CE and 0.91 A with HIS95.CD2; 20 ligand-proximal protein atoms lie within 3.0 A.
pipeline_breakers.mechanism: Confirms the benchmark is a true cryptic-site problem. It also means any geometric pocket-detection baseline (fpocket, CASTp) will score near zero on the apo input, which is exactly the classical-baseline comparison the challenge asks for.
pipeline_breakers.affects: Nothing negative; record it as the justification for a dynamics-based method.

search.method: RCSB search API, UniProt P01116 + exptl.method X-RAY DIFFRACTION -> 490 entries; batch GraphQL for sequence, alignment to P01116, non-polymer chem comps; residue 12 identity read through rcsb_polymer_entity_align.aligned_regions; drug-like defined as a non-polymer comp that is neither a guanine nucleotide nor a common ion/buffer and has formula weight > 200 Da

recommended_apo_replacement.title: Crystal Structure of a GDP-bound G12C Oncogenic Mutant of Human GTPase KRas
recommended_apo_replacement.crypticity_evidence: transplanted MOV clashes: 8 atoms < 2.0 A, 25 atoms < 3.0 A; closest HIS95.CD2 0.76 A, MET72.CE 0.80 A, CYS12.SG 1.40 A
recommended_apo_replacement.why: Deposited by the same group, in the same paper (DOI 10.1073/pnas.1404639111), released the same day as 4OBE (2014-06-04). 4OBE's own _pdbx_database_related record names 4LDJ with details 'G12C Kras' - the depositors themselves flag 4LDJ as the G12C structure and 4OBE as the wild-type companion. Higher resolution than 4OBE (1.15 vs 1.24 A), lower R-free (0.1622 vs 0.1686), one chain instead of two, no gaps, and 2 rather than 10 pocket residues in crystal contact.
recommended_apo_replacement.tradeoff: Only three of the four construct differences are removed: 4LDJ still retains native C51/C80/C118 whereas 6OIM is cysteine-light. It also departs from the literal challenge text, which names 4OBE.

other_apo_candidates.note: Highest resolution KRAS G12C apo structure found. Same packing exposure at the pocket as 4OBE, so it does not fix pipeline-breaker 3, but B-factors are not depressed. Title 'KRAS 1-169 G12C Mutant at 100k' - part of a multi-temperature series (8TXK 240K, 8TXJ 277K, 8TY2 293K, 8TY8 310K, 8TY9 313K), which is an interesting robustness set but each member must be checked separately.

This is the only apo entry whose construct exactly matches 6OIM (cysteine-light G12C), which would fix pipeline-breaker 2. But switch II residues 60-70 are unobserved, so 6 of the 21 pocket residues (60, 61, 62, 63, 68, 69) have no coordinates and cannot enter a contact network. Unusable.
Same problem: switch II 60-69 disordered, 6 of 21 pocket residues absent.

Carries fragment QWB (3-(imidazol-1-ylmethyl)-1H-indole). Its 4.5 A contact set is {5, 6, 7, 37, 39, 54, 55, 56, 71, 74, 75}, which has ZERO overlap with the 21-residue S-IIP set, so it is not an S-IIP occupancy problem - but it is a bound small molecule in the prediction input and should be avoided on principle.

holo_side.reason: 1.65 A, R-free 0.2152, all validation percentiles at or above median, single chain, monomeric assembly, zero crystal contacts at the pocket, both switches fully modelled, the covalent Cys12-MOV link explicit in _struct_conn, and the ligand chem comp (MOV) unambiguous. The 21-residue 4.5 A contact set matches the depositors' own _struct_site AC3 residue count of 21.

verdict.status: usable with documented caveats - but a substitution is strongly recommended
verdict.one_line: SUPERSEDED FRAMING: read 'blindness' as clause (iii) site-apo, not as the benchmark blind field - KRAS is not blind (ASBench HRAS AS001013301; Eren 2021 on 4OBE itself). The site-apo requirement is satisfied (the S-IIP is genuinely closed and ligand-free in 4OBE), but 4OBE is wild-type KRAS, not G12C, so the challenge's own apo/holo pair is not two forms of the same protein.
if_kept_as_is: State in the report that 4OBE is wild-type KRAS (evidence: _struct_ref_seq_dif has no mutation row; auth residue 12 is GLY).

SUPERSEDED by ADR 0007: residue 12 leaves the scoreable set by set membership (it is an active-site residue, with 11/13/16/34), not by ad-hoc exclusion. Its holo identity (CYS) still does not exist in the apo input.
Use chain A only; record the choice. Do not load both ASU copies.
Record the treatment of GDP and Mg2+ under C5.
Report the switch-II crystal-contact exposure (10 of 21 residues) as a limitation of the apo input.
verdict.recommended_action: Run 4LDJ as the primary apo input and keep 4OBE as a documented secondary/control run. Report both. 4LDJ is the same paper, same deposition day, higher resolution, actually G12C, and is named by 4OBE's own _pdbx_database_related record as the G12C structure. Because the challenge text fixes 4OBE, the 4OBE result must still be reported; the 4LDJ result is the scientifically defensible one and the delta between them is itself a result worth writing up.

constraint_impact.C1_apo_only: SATISFIED. No holo-derived information is present in 4OBE. The S-IIP is closed and unoccupied.
constraint_impact.C5_scope: RESOLVED in ADR 0006: cofactors are not network nodes; the apo entry own cofactor may locate the propagation source (ADR 0005).
constraint_impact.C6_elastic_network: Weakened for 4OBE by the lattice contacts on switch II; note as a limitation.

could_not_determine: Whether the challenge organisers intended 4LDJ and mistyped 4OBE, or deliberately chose the wild-type apo. Not derivable from any primary source.
The quantitative effect of the C51S / C80L / C118S construct difference on a contact network. Requires an experiment (build both networks, compare rankings); not answerable from metadata.

Literature residue ranges for Switch I and Switch II verbatim: Europe PMC returned HTTP 503 throughout this audit. The ranges used here are derived from UniProt P01116 annotations and from the _struct_conf / _struct_sheet_range records of the two files themselves.

Whether the depressed switch-II B-factors in 4OBE are caused by the crystal contacts. The two observations co-occur, but 8TVK has the same 10 contacts with a normal B ratio (0.95), so the correlation is not established.
